WebGL is part of 2 of my public repositories, from 2016 to 2026.

What it was for: [Science and visualisation](@/projects/science.md) (2).

Most recently: [algoglyph](@/work/algoglyph.md): Seeded, interactive p5.js plates: sorting, graphs, fractals, chaos, waves and gravity in 2D and 3D, each with measured readouts and a tested core; [maze](@/work/maze.md): Maze Web Application.

1 of these projects runs as a live site.

How to read the evidence: every [repository](@/glossary/repository.md) below is measured from GitHub and GitLab (every 6 hours) and says how it uses WebGL: as the main language, as a measured share of its code, in its declared stack or as a topic. The reference graph links WebGL to the repositories and to the other languages and technologies they use together.
